book.name: Egerton Gospel
book.title: Unknown Gospel · Egerton Papyrus 2 and Papyrus Köln VI 255
book.sourceNote: Public-domain English translation based on Andrew Bernhard's critical Greek text. Covenant preserves the four published manuscript-side boundaries and all printed lacuna markers.
book.identityNote: Fragmentary unidentified gospel represented by P.Egerton 2 with the associated Köln fragment. This reader does not reconstruct missing episodes or supply canonical parallels as text.
book.rights: The translator explicitly commits this English translation to the public domain and permits copying and modification for any purpose.

1.label: Fragment 1, verso
1.text: [...] to the lawyers ["...all] the wrongdoers [...] and not me [...] how does he do it?"

1.label: Fragment 1, verso
1.text: [Then he turned] to [the] rulers of the people and made this statement: "Search [the] scriptures; [you think] you have life in them. They [testify] about me. Don't [think] I've come to accuse [you] before my Father. [The one who accuses] you is Moses, in whom [you] hope."

1.label: Fragment 1, verso
1.text: But they [said,] "We know [well] God [spoke] to Moses, but you -- we don't know [where you're from."]

1.label: Fragment 1, verso
1.text: Jesus [told them] in reply, "Now [you] stand accused because [you don't believe those who've been approved] by him; because if [you believed Moses,] you'd believe [me, for] he [wrote] about me to your ancestors [...]"

2.label: Fragment 1, recto
2.text: [...] stones together [so they could stone him.] And the [rulers] laid their [hands] on him [so that] they might seize him and [deliver him] to the crowd. But they [could] not seize him, because the hour of his arrest [had] not yet [come.] So the Lord escaped [from their hands] and withdrew from [them.]

2.label: Fragment 1, recto
2.text: And look, someone with leprosy approached [him] and said, "Teacher Jesus, while I was [traveling] with [others] who had [leprosy] and eating at the inn [with them,] I [contracted leprosy] myself. But if [you want to,] you can cure me."

2.label: Fragment 1, recto
2.text: Now the Lord [told him, "I want to:] be cured." [And immediately] the leprosy left him.

2.label: Fragment 1, recto
2.text: Then Jesus [told] him, ["Go] and show [yourself] to the [priests] and offer [what Moses ordered for] your cure, and don't sin anymore [...]"

3.label: Fragment 2, recto
3.text: [...] to him, examining him to test him: "Teacher Jesus, we know that you've come [from God,] because the things you do [testify] above and beyond all the prophets. [So tell] us: is it right [to give] kings what belongs to them? [Should we pay] them, or [not?"]

3.label: Fragment 2, recto
3.text: But since Jesus knew what [they] were thinking, [he scolded them] and asked [them,] "Why do you pay me lip service as a Teacher but [don't do] what [I say? Isaiah] accurately prophesied [about] you when he said:

4.label: Fragment 2, verso
4.text: [...] enclosed in the [place ...] being subjected uncertainly [... its] weight unweighed [...] but [while] they were puzzled [as] to [his] strange question, Jesus walked and stood [on the] bank of the Jordan [river.] And reaching out with [his] right hand [...] and he sowed [on] the [...] and then [...] water [...] the [...] and [...] he produced [...] fruit [...]
